findings.title: Committing offsets from a background thread violates Kafka consumer thread-safety and can commit revoked partitions
findings.body: `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy` spawns a background thread (`self.commit_thread`) that periodically calls `self.commit_function(committable)`, which invokes Arroyo's `commit` callback on the underlying `KafkaConsumer`. Arroyo's `StreamProcessor` and `KafkaConsumer` are single-threaded and expect `commit` to be called only from `submit()`, `poll()`, or `join()` on the main consumer thread. Calling `commit` from a separate thread causes concurrent access to `KafkaConsumer` state (such as offset staging and `confluent_kafka` consumer calls) alongside `StreamProcessor._run_once()`. Furthermore, during a rebalance, `StreamProcessor` calls `strategy.close()`/`join()` and then revokes partitions; because `close()` stops `commit_thread` *before* draining `queue_pool` and does not perform a final commit, offsets completed while draining aren't committed, or if `commit_thread` is still running it can call `commit` for partitions after they have been revoked. Offset commits should be performed in `poll()` and `join()` on the strategy's caller thread rather than a background thread.

findings.title: Sharing `FixedQueuePool` on the strategy factory breaks consumer rebalances
findings.body: `ResultsStrategyFactory.__init__` creates a single `FixedQueuePool` instance (`self.queue_pool`) and passes it into `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy` in `create_with_partitions()`. When a Kafka consumer group rebalance occurs, Arroyo closes the active strategy—which calls `self.queue_pool.shutdown()`—and then calls `factory.create_with_partitions()` again for the new assignment. Because `shutdown()` permanently stops all `OrderedQueueWorker` threads and shuts down all `queue.Queue` instances (raising `queue.ShutDown` on subsequent `put()` calls), and because `OffsetTracker` retains stale offset history from the previous assignment (`last_committed`, `all_offsets`, `outstanding`), the consumer will fail to enqueue or process any messages after the first rebalance. A fresh `FixedQueuePool` (or per-strategy worker/tracker state) needs to be created per `create_with_partitions` lifecycle, or `FixedQueuePool` must not be shut down by `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close()`/`terminate()` while its `OffsetTracker` is reset for the new partition assignment.

findings.title: Unbounded work queues provide no backpressure and can exhaust memory
findings.body: `FixedQueuePool.__init__` initializes each `work_queue` as an unbounded `queue.Queue()` (`maxsize=0`). Although `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy`'s docstring states "Natural backpressure when queues fill up", `work_queue.put(work_item)` in `FixedQueuePool.submit` will never block or raise `Arroyo`'s `MessageRejected`. The main Kafka consumer thread will continue polling and decoding messages at full speed even if worker threads are slow or blocked on I/O, buffering an unbounded number of `WorkItem` objects (including full decoded payloads and raw Kafka messages) in memory until the process runs out of memory.

findings.title: `FixedQueuePool.shutdown` abandons queued items instead of draining them
findings.body: In `FixedQueuePool.shutdown()`, `worker.shutdown = True` is set on every worker before calling `q.shutdown(immediate=False)`. Because `OrderedQueueWorker.run()` checks `while not self.shutdown:`, each worker exits its loop as soon as it finishes the single item it is currently processing, leaving all remaining items sitting in `work_queue` unprocessed (even though `immediate=False` was passed to `q.shutdown()`). In addition, `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close()` stops `commit_thread` *before* calling `self.queue_pool.shutdown()`, so even the in-flight items that finish during `queue_pool.shutdown()` never have their offsets committed.

findings.title: Non-contiguous Kafka offsets (e.g. compacted topics or transactions) permanently stall offset commits
findings.body: `OffsetTracker.get_committable_offsets` iterates `for offset in range(start, max_offset + 1):` and breaks as soon as an integer `offset` is not in `all_offsets`. After the first commit sets `last_committed`, `start` becomes `last_committed + 1`. If Kafka ever delivers non-consecutive offsets on a partition—which happens when control records/transactions are present, after log compaction, or if a wrapper strategy filters a message before `submit()`—`last_committed + 1` will never be added to `all_offsets`, and `get_committable_offsets` will never advance commits for that partition again, causing `all_offsets` to grow without bound. Since Kafka delivers messages in offset order per partition, tracking seen offsets in order (or iterating `sorted(all_offsets)` rather than `range(start, max_offset + 1)`) avoids assuming every integer offset exists.
